requirements.quote: Streams are identified by an unsigned 31-bit integer.  Streams
requirements.condition: When representing or processing an HTTP/2 stream identifier.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an unsigned 31-bit integer as the stream identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use values or representations outside the unsigned 31-bit range.
requirements.why_checkable: The representation and numeric range of every stream identifier can be inspected or tested.

requirements.quote: initiated by a client MUST use odd-numbered stream identifiers; those
requirements.condition: When a client initiates a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an odd-numbered stream identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use an even-numbered stream identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect the parity of identifiers assigned to client-initiated streams.

requirements.quote: initiated by the server MUST use even-numbered stream identifiers.  A
requirements.condition: When a server initiates a stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Use an even-numbered stream identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use an odd-numbered stream identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect the parity of identifiers assigned to server-initiated streams.

requirements.quote:
stream identifier of zero (0x00) is used for connection control
   messages; the stream identifier of zero cannot be used to establish a
   new stream.
requirements.condition: When selecting a stream identifier for a connection-control message.
requirements.required_behavior: Use stream identifier zero where the connection-control message is defined to use the connection-control stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Encoded connection-control messages can be checked for stream identifier zero.

requirements.quote:
messages; the stream identifier of zero cannot be used to establish a
   new stream.
requirements.condition: When establishing a new stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use stream identifier zero.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can attempt to establish a stream with identifier zero and verify that it is not treated as a new stream.

requirements.quote:
The identifier of a newly established stream MUST be numerically
   greater than all streams that the initiating endpoint has opened or
   reserved.  This governs streams that are opened using a HEADERS frame
   and streams that are reserved using PUSH_PROMISE.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint establishes a stream using HEADERS or reserves a stream using PUSH_PROMISE.
requirements.required_behavior: Choose an identifier numerically greater than every stream identifier that endpoint has previously opened or reserved.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not establish or reserve a stream with an identifier less than or equal to any identifier that the initiating endpoint has already opened or reserved.
requirements.why_checkable: The new identifier can be compared with the initiating endpoint's history of opened and reserved identifiers.

requirements.quote:
and streams that are reserved using PUSH_PROMISE.  An endpoint that
   receives an unexpected stream identifier MUST respond with a
   connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives an unexpected stream identifier.
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A malformed identifier sequence can be injected and the resulting connection error and code observed.

requirements.quote:
A HEADERS frame will transition the client-initiated stream
   identified by the stream identifier in the frame header from "idle"
   to "open".
requirements.condition: When a HEADERS frame identifies an idle client-initiated stream in its frame header.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition that stream from "idle" to "open".
requirements.why_checkable: The stream state before and after processing the HEADERS frame can be observed.

requirements.quote:
to "open".  A PUSH_PROMISE frame will transition the server-initiated
   stream identified by the Promised Stream ID field in the frame
   payload from "idle" to "reserved (local)" or "reserved (remote)".
requirements.condition: When a PUSH_PROMISE frame identifies an idle server-initiated stream in its Promised Stream ID field.
requirements.required_behavior: Transition that stream from "idle" to the appropriate "reserved (local)" or "reserved (remote)" state.
requirements.why_checkable: The promised stream's state can be inspected after processing PUSH_PROMISE.

requirements.quote:
When a stream transitions out of the "idle" state, all streams in the
   "idle" state that might have been opened by the peer with a lower-
   valued stream identifier immediately transition to "closed".
requirements.condition: When a stream transitions out of the "idle" state.
requirements.required_behavior: Immediately transition every lower-valued idle stream that the peer might have opened to "closed".
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not leave such a skipped lower-valued stream in "idle" or permit it to be opened later.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can skip identifiers and inspect the states of all lower-valued peer streams immediately after the transition.

requirements.quote: Stream identifiers cannot be reused.  Long-lived connections can
requirements.condition: After a stream identifier has been used on a connection.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse that stream identifier on the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Identifier allocation and frame traces can be checked for reuse over the lifetime of a connection.

requirements.quote:
a SETTINGS frame.  The maximum concurrent streams setting is specific
   to each endpoint and applies only to the peer that receives the
   setting.
requirements.condition: When SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS is sent by an endpoint.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the setting only to the peer that receives it.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply the setting as a shared or sender-side limit.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can advertise distinct limits in each direction and observe which endpoint's stream creation is constrained.

requirements.quote:
setting.  That is, clients specify the maximum number of concurrent
   streams the server can initiate, and servers specify the maximum
   number of concurrent streams the client can initiate.
requirements.condition: When a client advertises SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret it as the maximum number of concurrent streams the server can initiate.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interpret it as limiting streams the client initiates.
requirements.why_checkable: Direction-specific stream creation can be exercised after a client advertises a limit.

requirements.quote:
setting.  That is, clients specify the maximum number of concurrent
   streams the server can initiate, and servers specify the maximum
   number of concurrent streams the client can initiate.
requirements.condition: When a server advertises SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret it as the maximum number of concurrent streams the client can initiate.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interpret it as limiting streams the server initiates.
requirements.why_checkable: Direction-specific stream creation can be exercised after a server advertises a limit.

requirements.quote:
Streams that are in the "open" state or in either of the "half-
   closed" states count toward the maximum number of streams that an
   endpoint is permitted to open.  Streams in any of these three states
   count toward the limit advertised in the
   SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS setting.
requirements.condition: When calculating usage of an advertised SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Count streams in "open", "half-closed (local)", and "half-closed (remote)" states toward the limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit streams in any of those three states from the count.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can place streams in each named state and inspect whether each contributes to the concurrency count.

requirements.quote:
SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS setting.  Streams in either of the
   "reserved" states do not count toward the stream limit.
requirements.condition: When calculating usage of an advertised SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Exclude streams in either reserved state from the count.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not count "reserved (local)" or "reserved (remote)" streams toward the limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can create reserved streams and verify that they do not consume concurrency capacity.

requirements.quote: Endpoints MUST NOT exceed the limit set by their peer.  An endpoint
requirements.condition: When an endpoint opens streams subject to its peer's concurrent-stream limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the applicable concurrent-stream count at or below the peer's limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not exceed the limit set by the peer.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can advertise a low limit and count the endpoint's concurrently active streams.

requirements.quote:
that receives a HEADERS frame that causes its advertised concurrent
   stream limit to be exceeded MUST treat this as a stream error
   (Section 5.4.2) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR or REFUSED_STREAM.
requirements.condition: When receiving a HEADERS frame causes the receiver's advertised concurrent-stream limit to be exceeded.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the condition as a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR or REFUSED_STREAM.
requirements.why_checkable: A HEADERS frame can be sent beyond the advertised limit and the stream-scoped error code observed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint that wishes to reduce the value of
   SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS to a value that is below the current
   number of open streams can either close streams that exceed the new
   value or allow streams to complete.
requirements.condition: When reducing SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS below the current number of open streams.
requirements.required_behavior: Either close streams exceeding the new value or allow existing streams to complete.
requirements.why_checkable: The handling of already-open streams can be observed after the endpoint advertises a lower limit.

requirements.quote:
interfere with each other.  Flow control is used for both individual
   streams and the connection as a whole.
requirements.condition: When implementing HTTP/2 flow control.
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain flow control for individual streams and separately for the connection as a whole.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can independently exhaust and update stream-level and connection-level flow-control windows.

requirements.quote:
HTTP/2 provides for flow control through use of the WINDOW_UPDATE
   frame (Section 6.9).
requirements.condition: When increasing flow-control credit.
requirements.required_behavior: Use WINDOW_UPDATE frames as the protocol mechanism for flow-control updates.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame traces can verify that flow-control credit is updated through WINDOW_UPDATE.

requirements.quote:
1.  Flow control is specific to a connection.  HTTP/2 flow control
       operates between the endpoints of a single hop and not over the
       entire end-to-end path.
requirements.condition: When maintaining HTTP/2 flow-control state.
requirements.required_behavior: Scope flow control to one connection between endpoints of a single hop.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not apply one connection's flow-control state across the entire end-to-end path.
requirements.why_checkable: Implementations with multiple hops or connections can be tested for independent flow-control state.

requirements.quote:
2.  Flow control is based on WINDOW_UPDATE frames.  Receivers
       advertise how many octets they are prepared to receive on a
       stream and for the entire connection.  This is a credit-based
       scheme.
requirements.condition: When a receiver advertises available flow-control credit.
requirements.required_behavior: Advertise octet credit for each stream and for the entire connection using WINDOW_UPDATE-based flow control.
requirements.why_checkable: WINDOW_UPDATE values and the corresponding stream and connection credit accounting can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
3.  Flow control is directional with overall control provided by the
       receiver.  A receiver MAY choose to set any window size that it
       desires for each stream and for the entire connection.
requirements.condition: When a receiver selects flow-control windows.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the receiver to choose window sizes independently for each stream and for the entire connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests can advertise different valid stream and connection window sizes and verify they are honored.

requirements.quote:
desires for each stream and for the entire connection.  A sender
       MUST respect flow-control limits imposed by a receiver.
requirements.condition: When a sender transmits data subject to receiver-advertised flow control.
requirements.required_behavior: Respect all flow-control limits imposed by the receiver.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send flow-controlled data beyond the receiver's available credit.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can constrain advertised credit and measure whether the sender transmits beyond it.

requirements.quote:
MUST respect flow-control limits imposed by a receiver.  Clients,
       servers, and intermediaries all independently advertise their
       flow-control window as a receiver and abide by the flow-control
       limits set by their peer when sending.
requirements.condition: When a client, server, or intermediary acts as a receiver and sender.
requirements.required_behavior: Independently advertise its receiver-side flow-control window and abide by its peer's flow-control limits when sending.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not substitute locally advertised receive limits for the peer's send limits.
requirements.why_checkable: Bidirectional tests can compare each participant's advertised receive window with its independent outbound sending behavior.

requirements.quote:
4.  The initial value for the flow-control window is 65,535 octets
       for both new streams and the overall connection.
requirements.condition: When a new stream's flow-control window is initialized.
requirements.required_behavior: Initialize the stream flow-control window to 65,535 octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a different initial stream window absent a protocol-defined update.
requirements.why_checkable: The amount of DATA initially permitted on a new stream can be measured.

requirements.quote:
4.  The initial value for the flow-control window is 65,535 octets
       for both new streams and the overall connection.
requirements.condition: When the connection-level flow-control window is initialized.
requirements.required_behavior: Initialize the connection flow-control window to 65,535 octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a different initial connection window.
requirements.why_checkable: The amount of DATA initially permitted across the connection can be measured.

requirements.quote:
5.  The frame type determines whether flow control applies to a
       frame.  Of the frames specified in this document, only DATA
       frames are subject to flow control; all other frame types do not
       consume space in the advertised flow-control window.
requirements.condition: When sending or receiving a DATA frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply flow-control accounting to the DATA frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transmit DATA beyond the applicable advertised flow-control windows.
requirements.why_checkable: Window accounting can be inspected before and after DATA frames.

requirements.quote:
5.  The frame type determines whether flow control applies to a
       frame.  Of the frames specified in this document, only DATA
       frames are subject to flow control; all other frame types do not
       consume space in the advertised flow-control window.
requirements.condition: When sending or receiving any frame type other than DATA.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave the advertised flow-control window unchanged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not consume flow-control-window space for a non-DATA frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Window values can be compared before and after each non-DATA frame type.

requirements.quote:
6.  An endpoint can choose to disable its own flow control, but an
       endpoint cannot ignore flow-control signals from its peer.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint chooses to disable its own receiver-side flow control.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue to honor flow-control signals received from its peer.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not ignore the peer's flow-control signals.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can disable local receive-side restrictions, vary peer-advertised credit, and verify outbound transmission still follows that credit.
